A.K.M. Shahidul Huq, J: On an  application under Article 102(2) of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh made by the petitioners this Court on 15.11.2015 issued a Rule Nisi calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned advertisement dated 18.06.2015 published in the Daily Ittefaq pursuant to memo no. 12.01.0000.38.11.003.2015/6945 dated 17.06.2015 (Annexure-D) issued by the respondent no. 2 so far it relates to appointment in the post of "Farm Labour" (Serial no. 9 of the advertisement) without absorbing and regularizing the petitioners in the revenue budget, in the department of Agricultural Extension under the Ministry of Agricultural with arrear salaries, allowances, house rent and other admissible service benefits from the date of their joining in the service and onwards, shall not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and of no legal effect and further to show cause as to why direction shall not be given upon the respondents to absorb and regularize the service of the petitioners as “Farm Labour” min the revenue budget considering their length of service in the said department and also pursuant to the memo no. Krishi-May-2/84/283 dated 28.05.1984 (Annexure-B Series) issued under the authority of the respondent no. 1 and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to the disposal of the rule are that, the respondents are the public servants performing functions in connection with the affairs of the Republic and the addresses of the respondents as mentioned in the cause title are correct for servicing notices of the Hon'ble Court upon them. The Government of Bangladesh has tried to follow the course of planned development in the field of agriculture and launched 'Five Year Plan' on different times with a view of achieve goal in agriculture and for the rapid development in the field of agriculture our Government had also given most emphasis upon it and hence established the Department of Agriculture Extension under the Ministry of Agriculture. The petitioners were appointed as the `Irregular Labours' in the different Horticulture Centres of the Department of Agriculture Extension under the Ministry of Agriculture on the different occasions. The petitioner no. 01 was appointed as Irregular Labour in 1999 and he was appointed as Regular Labour on 01.07.2003. The petitioner no. 02 was appointed as Irregular Labour in 2004 and he was appointed as Regular Labour on 01.01.2007. The petitioner no. 03 was appointed as Irregular Labour on 01.01.2000 and he was appointed as Regular Labour on 01.07.2009. The petitioner no. 04 was appointed as Irregular Labour in 2005 and he was appointed as Regular Labour on 01.10.2009. The petitioner nos. 05 and 06 were appointed as Irregular Labours on 01.01.2005 who were appointed as Regular Labours on 01.01.2009. The petitioner no. 07 was appointed as Irregular Labour on 01.01.2003 and he was appointed as Regular Labour on 01.09.2009. The petitioner no. 08 was appointed as Irregular Labour in 2005 who was appointed as Regular Labour on 09.01.2013 and all of them are still serving as `Regular Master Roll Labours' in the department of Agricultural Extension with their utmost diligence and sincerity and they are given salary from the Labour Allowance Code no. DAE-4851. 

 3. As per the Circulars vide the memo nos. কৃম/শা-১/সঃ-৭১/২০০৩/১৭২৫ dated 27.11.2005, কৃষি-৩/বে-৬/৮৯(ভলি-১)/৪৩ dated 23.01.1990 and নং-কৃষি-মে-২/৮৪/২৮৩   dated 28.05.1984 issued by the Ministry of and the memo no. ২-আর-১১/৯২(II)১২৫৫৫(৩) dated 02.12.2008 and  ১এস-৬৮৫/৫০৯৮(১৬৫)dated 18.04.1990 issued by the Office of the Director General, the Department of the Agricultural Extension some of the Regular Master Roll Labour of the same category have been absorbed and regularized in the revenue budget as 'Farm Labour' on the different occasions but unfortunately the present petitioners were not absorbed in the revenue budget till date who are the victims of discrimination and arbitrary decision. The petitioners on the different occasions made representations to the respondents for absorption their service in the revenue budget as 'Farm Labour' and officially the matter was placed before the concern authority on several times but no fruitful result comes out and as such the necessary directions may be given upon the respondents for transferring their service in the revenue budget. An advertisement has been published in 'The Daily Ittefaq' on 18.06.2015 inviting applications for appointment of the 'Farm Labour' (Serial no. 09 in the advertisement) in the 390 posts vide the memo no. 12.01.0000.38.11.003.2015/ 6945 dated 17.06.2015 on behalf of the Director General, Department of the Agricultural Extension, Khamar Bari, Farmgate, Dhaka (respondent no. 02) and the process of the said appointment is still pending. The petitioners are very much afraid of presuming that their service would be ended after completion of the abovementioned appointment and their future lives shall be difficult to survive. The Government has already transferred some of the Regular Master Roll Labours to the revenue budget as 'Farm Labour' on 12.04.2009, 05.02.2009 and 20.02.2008 who are standing on the similar footing of the petitioners and as such the services of the petitioners are also liable to be transferred to the revenue set up as 'Farm Labour' without any further delay otherwise they shall be highly prejudiced. On behalf of the petitioners a Notice Demanding Justice was served on 14.09.2015 upon the respondents requesting them to absorb the services of the petitioners as 'Farm Labour' in the revenue budget but no response is found till to day. The petitioners nos. 2-8 have executed a Letter of Authority in favour of the petitioner no. 01 to swear affidavit and also to conduct this writ petition on behalf of the petitioners no. 2-8. 

 4. The agriculture is the main strength of our economy and our prosperity is mostly depends on the development of agriculture and our Government is trying its best to achieve the ultimate goal of the 'Five years Plan' and it was successful. The manpower of the different Horticulture Centres under the Department of the Agricultural Extension are trained up as experts and efficient to carry on any Horticultural activities and indeed they are very necessary manpower and as such considering the practical aspects and their importance, their services should be transferred to the revenue set up and hence the necessary directions may kindly be passed upon the respondents to transfer their services under the revenue budget of the Government. 

 6. Mr. Md. Kofil Udin Khan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the some of the Regular Master Roll Labours of the similar category have been absorbed and regularized in the revenue budget as 'Farm Labour' who are on the similar footing of the petitioners and hence they are entitled to be transferred in the revenue budget as 'Farm Labour' as such the necessary directions may kindly be given upon the respondents to absorb the services of the petitioners under the revenue budget of the Government maintaining continuity from the respective date of their joining in service with all other service benefits. 

 7. The learned Advocate next submits that the petitioners have served more than 10 years in the their service with utmost sincerity and diligence and at present most of them are running 35 to 45 years and now they have got no scope to join in the Government/Non-Government service as they are already barred by their age and since in the field of agriculture, there are scarcity of experienced and expert manpower like the petitioners and since in the meantime the petitioners have approached to the proper authorities with various applications/representations on several times but no fruitful result comes out and as such the necessary directions may kindly be passed upon the respondents to absorb and regularize their services under the revenue budget of the Government with all service benefits. 

 8. He further submits that the petitioners have satisfactory service record and they have requisite qualifications and they are serving as the Master Roll employees for the welfare and wellbeing of the nation at large and exhausted their youth with dedication and devotion relying on the promise of their appointing authority and hence the petitioners have acquired vested rights and it is their genuine legitimate expectation to be absorbed and regularized in the revenue set up and as such the Government is under an obligation to transfer their services in the revenue budget. 

 9. He also submits that the service of the some employees of the similar posts have been transferred to the post of 'Farm Labour' and absorbed in the revenue budget earlier but unfortunately the petitioners have not been considered to absorb in the revenue budget though 390 posts are vacant and they are the victims of clear discrimination because of the malafide and arbitrary acts of the respondents on the basis of pick and choose and as such the respondents may kindly be directed to absorb and regularize of the service of the petitioners in the Revenue Budget as 'Farm Labour' with arrear salaries, allowances, house rent, time scale and other admissible service benefits. 

 10. He lastly submits that at the time of appointment of the petitioners, the respondent no. 2 promised to the petitioners that later on their service would be transferred to the revenue budget mentioning the Circular issued by the Ministry of Agriculture vide the Memo no. কৃষি-/১মে-২/৮৪/২৮৩ dated 28.05.1984 and they relied on it but unfortunately their legitimate rights are ignoring by the respondents arbitrarily though they are legally bound by the doctrine of promissory estoppels and the petitioners are entitled to be absorbed in the revenue budget and as such the respondents may kindly be directed by Your Lordships to absorb their services in the revenue budget as 'Farm Labour' with all admissible service benefits. Hence it is liable to be absolute. 

 13. He next submits that the regular labour cannot be absorbed in Revenue Budget as Firm Labour and this type of absorption will create problem in the service and as such alleged absorption as an firm labour of the petitioners not possible as per law. 

 15. We have perused the writ petition filed under article 102 (2) of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and the annexures filed that heard the learned Advocate for the petitioner considered the submissions as advanced by the learned Advocate for the petitioner on perusal of the impugned annexures filed there to on perusal of the same we find illegality, irregularity in the said impugned annexure. The words "legitimate expectation" was first coined by Lord Denning in the case of Schmidt Vs. Secretary of State for Home Affairs, (1969) 2 Ch 149. But this phrase was limited at that time, first of all to a legal right which was contravened. Changed view is that where expectations were not legally enforceable but had some reasonable basis, were treated as legitimate expectations. But it has by now established as a principle of law. This principle in essence imposes a duty to act fairly and requires of the concerned authorities to act reasonably in dealing with the rights and interest of the people in the given circumstances. If the situation so demands, the Court shall certainly strike down such orders in exercise of its powers of judicial review of executive actions. In case of their unreasonableness or inertness or even latches on their part for which some benefit is lost causing prejudice to the people at large or even to an individual, the Court may also direct the concerned authorities to exercise their functions fairly, reasonably and in accordance with law. 

 "It is for the council and not for this Court to determine what the future policy should be in relation to the number of taxi licences which are to be issued in the City of Liverpool. It is not for this Court to consider population growths or falls or the extent of the demand for taxis within or without the city or whether there should be more licences issued in the future than in the past or whether the present grave unemployment position on Merseyside is a relevant consideration. All those are matters for the council. This Court is concerned to see that whatever policy the corporation adopts is adopted after due and fair regard to all the conflicting interest. The power of the court to intervene is not limited, as once was thought, to those cases where the function in question is judicial or quasi-judicial. The modern cases show that this Court will intervene more widely than in the past. Even where the function is said to be administrative, the Court will not hesitate to intervene in a suitable case if it is necessary in order to secure fairness." 

 "The doctrine of "legitimate expectation" has an important place in the developing law of judicial review. It is, however, not necessary to explore the doctrine in this case, it is enough merely to note that a legitimate expectation can provide a sufficient interest to enable one who cannot point to the existence of a substantive right to obtain the leave of the Court to apply for judicial review." 

 30. The question of legitimate expectation was also considered by the Supreme Court of India in a number of case. In the case of Navjyoti Coo-Group Housing Society Vs. Union of India AIR 1993 (SC) 155, the criterion for allotment of land to the Co-operative Group Housing Societies on the basis of the date of registration of such Societies was changed by the impugned memorandum to one on the basis of the date of approval of the final list by the Registrar. The Delhi High Court indicated that in view of long standing practice the office memorandum laying down a completely different criterion should have been made public and further held the said memorandum as arbitrary and unreasonable and struck it down. Although the Government withdrew the impugned memorandum but in disposing of the Special Leave Petition, the Supreme court of India upheld the principle of "legitimate expectation" as enshrined by the I louse of Lords in the case of CCSU Vs. Minister for Civil Service. GN Ray, J held as follows: 

 The Group Housing Societies if necessary by way of a public notice so that they might take proper representation to the concerned authorities for consideration of their view points. Even assuming that in the absence of any explanation of the expression "first come first served" in Rule 6(vi) of Nazrul Rules there was no statutory requirement to make allotment with reference to date of registration, it has been rightly held, as a matter of fact, by the High Court that prior to the new guideline contained in the memo of January 20, 1990 the principle for allotment had always been on the basis of date of Registration and not the date of approval of the list of members. In the brochure issued in 1982 by the DDA even after Gazette Notification of Nazrul Rules on September 26, 1981 the policy of allotment on the basis of seniority in registration was clearly indicated. In the aforesaid facts, the Group I-lousing Societies were entitled to 'legitimate expectation' of following consistent past practice in the matter." 

 32. In the case of the Chief Engineer of Local Government and Engineering Department and others Vs. Kazi Mizanur Rahman and 8 others reported in 17 BLC AD page 91 where our Apex Court explained the principle of Legitimate Expectation very elaborately. 

 "The doctrine of legitimate expectation is a concept which is akin to that a promissory estoppels and this concept has been developed in the European Community of Law. According to the doctrine where a person is a victim of an unfavourable decision taken by a public authority this may amount to an infringement of that persons legitimate expectation, where for example the decision contradicts an earlier promise or course of conduct on the part of the public authority concerned. Therefore this doctrine is circumscribed by certain limitations and exceptions. The first and foremost consideration is that there must be a foundation in the petition claiming legitimate expectation and secondly there must be a promise or a representation on the part of the public on the claim of the person aggrieved by the decision. In this connection it will be very much pertinent to reiterate an observation of the Supreme Court of India in the case of National Building Construction Corporations Vs Raghunathan reported in AIR 1998 SC page 2779 held that:- 

 "Incidentally in this case what question of Legitimate Expectation and not raised in the petition and foundation was laid in the pleadings for such a plea being advanced before the Court. Strangely the High Court allowed this plea at the stage of argument and allowed the petitions only on the ground of Legitimate Expectation without least realizing that there was hardly any legitimacy in the claim of the respondents. In the absence of pleading and the affidavit of the respondents and support thereof the whole exercise done by the High Court cannot be but be termed to be speculation."

 36. Similar views were taken by our Apex Court in the case of Bangladesh Textile Mills Corporation Vs. Nasir Ahmed Chowdhury, reported in 7 MLR AD page 265 which runs as follows:- 

 37. In this case this Division approved the views taken in the case of Hindustan Development Corporation. The Court will not interfere on the ground of procedural fairness to a person whose interest based on legitimate expectation might be affected. 

 38. On due and proper consideration and the principles as laid down in the case of LGED vs. Mizanur Rahman our Apex Court has laid down certain guidelines on the principle of Legitimate Expectation after reviewing all previous judgments and rules in order to settle the principles of law as regards Legitimate Expectation which sum up under; 

 I)	Whenever any vacancy in LGED is created in the revenue set up it shall consider for absorption of employees or officers of the development projects within the meaning of section 2 (ga) of the Rules, 2005 if the project in which she/he is working is completed subject to the condition that such employee or officer has requisite qualifications for the said post. 

 II)	Whenever a vacant post is created in the revenue budget, the LGED shall absorb/transfer any employee or officer from the development project mentioned in clause (i) to fill up that post in accordance with Rules of 1985 and the ECNEC's decision dated le January, 2008. 

 III)	An officer or employee shall be absorbed if she was appointed in the development project within the meaning or rule 2(Ka) of Rules 2005 in accordance with the procedures prescribed for appointment in public employment. 

 IV)	An officer or employee must have requisite qualifications for the post in which he is seeking absorption. 

 V)	An officer or employee must have continuity service in the project in which he is working. 

 VI)	An officer or employee must have satisfactory service record before his case is considered for regularization in the revenue budget. 

 VII)	If an officer and employee whose rank and status does not relate to the posts advertised by the impugned notifications on the day of its publications, such officer or employee would not be eligible for consideration for absorption. 

 VIII)	The employees and officers who have been working in the development projects mentioned in clause (I) on monthly pay basis would only be eligible for consideration for absorption in the revenue budget. 

 IX)	Unless and until vacancies in the revenue budget in the LGED are created the employees and officers of the development project mentioned in clause (I) can not claim as of right to be absorbed in the revenue budget. 

 X)	While considering and selecting an employee or officer of the development project for absorption in the revenue budget, the appointing authority shall maintain strictly the prevailing quota system for employment in the public employment being followed by the Government. 

 XI)	The LGED shall consider the case of those working on master roll basis for absorption in the revenue by phases if they have requisite qualifications subject to the availability of vacancies according to their seniority. 

 39. On the similar point our Apex Court in the case of Bangladesh Rural Development Board BRDB represented by its Director General Vs. Md. Mahbub Alam Khan and others held that the High Court Division came to a finding that in order to facilitate absorption of the personnel of development project the Government promulgated SRO No. 182-A in/2005/Shomo/Bidhi-l/S-9/2000 dated 20.06.2005 making clear and specific provisions to absorb all the personnel of development projects which started between 9th April, 1972 to 30th June, 1997. In the instant case, the project of the writ-petitioners started in July, 1993 and they are entitled to be absorbed under the revenue budget pursuant to the provisions of that SRO. The High Court Division further held that the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) at its meeting dated 31.12.2001 had taken decision to transfer all the personnel of the development projects expeditiously to the revenue budget and that the decision was circulated by the Planning Division by the memo dated 10.01.2008 asking all concerned to take necessary steps to transfer all completed development projects to the revenue budget. 

 40. The High Court Division considered the case of Bangladesh Vs. Md. Abul Hossain, (2003) BLD (AD) 129 in which this Division held that once a privilege is given to a person on condition of doing any act and if such condition is fulfilled and continues to be fulfilled, such privilege or right cannot be taken away or cancelled without giving a chance of being heard. 

 41. Therefore, the High Court Division directed the leave-petitioners to absorb or regularize the writ-petitioners in the regular set up of the Local Government and Rural Development and Co-operatives under the leave-petitioners in permanent post as and when vacancy would arise subject to the condition that they are not otherwise disqualified. 

 44. The High Court Division in arriving its decision in the instant case relying the decisions reported in 1 WLR page 1482, 2AC 629 and number of reported decisions of All England Reports.

 "The Government took the decision on agreement to release the mill in question lack of power on the part of the Government so to do is not the plea, rather a belated plea was taken that the decision has been revised by the Government although no such case was made out. Hence applying the aforesaid principle the least that can be said is that the respondents can not be allowed to act inconsistently and the decision to release the mill remains binding on them. Mahbub Alam Khan and others vs. Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Local Government Rural Development and Co-operations the Division Bench of the Hon'ble High Court Division while deciding the Writ Petition No. 7484 of 2009 on 17.01.2012 held that the petitioners cannot be discriminated and the respondents cannot adopt a pick and chose policy. By working for a reasonable period of time the petitioners have all acquired, skills and expertise and can legitimately expect that they will be absorbed. Having served for long years and in view of the past practice the petitioners can reasonably expect that they will be absorbed in the revenue budget. In this connection reliance is placed on the case of Attorney General of Hong Kong Vs. Ng Tuen Shik 2 AC 629 a leading case on the doctrine of Legitimate Expectation wherein Lord Fraser Said:- 

 51. The doctrine of legitimate expectation and its impact in the administrative law has been considered by our court. Explaining the nature and scope of doctrine of legitimate expectation in the case of Bangladesh Vs. Md. Abdul Hossain reported in 2003 BUD (AD) 129. The Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh held that once a privilege is given to a person on condition of doing any act and if such condition is fulfilled such privilege or right can not be taken away or cancelled without giving a chance of being heard. 

 55. The impugned advertisement dated 18.06.2015 published in the Daily Ittefaq pursuant to memo no. 12.01.0000. 38.11.003.2015/6945 dated 17.06.2015 (Annexure-E) to the writ petition issued by the respondent no. 2 so far it relates to appointment in the post of "Farm Labour" (Serial no. 9 of the said advertisement) without absorbing and regularizing the petitioner in the revenue budget, in the department of Agricultural Extension under the Ministry of Agricultural with arrear salaries, allowances, house rent and other admissible service benefits from the date of his joining in the service and onwards, is hereby declared to have been made without lawful authority and of no legal effect. 

 56. The respondent no. 2 is hereby directed to absorb and regularize the service of the petitioner as 'Farm Labour' in the revenue budget considering his length of service in the aforesaid department pursuant to the memo no. Krishi-/lMay-2/84/283 dated 28.05.1994 (Annexure-B series) issued under the authority of the respondent no. 01 in accordance with law within 1 month from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment positively.
